Box 2754, Bangkok 10501, Thailand (Received 23 August 1994; revised version received 6 December 1995; accepted 20 December 1995) Abstract The feasibility of thermophilic (55) anaerobic treat- ment of an alcohol distillery wastewater (cane molasses vinasse) was studied using a 140 l upflow anaerobic sludge blanket (UASB) reactor for a period of 430 days. Organic loading rates were applied up to 28 kg chemical oxygen demand (COD) m-3 d1 by reducing hydraulic retention time (HRT) at a fixed influent concentration of 10 g COD 1-1. Chemical oxy- gen demand removals during the entire experimental period were relatively low (39-67%), while biochemi- cal oxygen demand (BOD) removals were more satisfactory (more than 80%). The biodegradability of the vinasse used in this study was assessed by a serum vial test. The test revealed that methane production rates from the vinasse were only 1/36, 1/32, 1/25 and 1/23 as great as those from H2/C02, acetate, glucose and another type of vinasse (malt), respectively. The poor performance of the reactor for COD elimination can probably be attributed to the low degradability of the waste itself Methanogenic activity of the retained sludge increased 24 times, for acetate, and 13 times, for H2/C02, as much as that of the inoculum sludge. The optimum temperature of methanogenic activity of the sludge depended on the substrate used; i.e. 60~C for acetate, 60-65 for H2/COe, and around 55 for the waste. Copyright 1996 Elsevier Science Ltd. Key words: Vinasse, thermophilic anaerobic diges- tion, upflow anaerobic sludge blanket reactor, granular sludge, biodegradability. INTRODUCTION In recent years, the upflow anaerobic sludge blanket (USAB) process has been successfully used for the *Author to whom correspondence should be addressed. 215 treatment of various types of wastewaters (Lettinga & Hulshoff Pol, 1991). However, most of the full- scale UASB plants constructed so far have employed mesophilic treatment systems and, to our best know- ledge, there is at present only one pilot-scale (70 m3) thermophilic UASB plant in operation, in Brazil, treating sugar-cane vinasse. The thermophilic pilot-plant was used at an applied volumetric COD loading of 25-30 kg COD m-3 d-1 with the COD removal above 70% (Souza et al., 1992). Heat processing in certain kinds of agro-indus- tries, such as alcohol distillery, canning and pulp production, discharges high-temperature wastes with a high COD strength. These wastes usually contain poorly biodegradable or toxic organic matters, such as phenolic compounds, leading to a low COD treat- ment capacity for anaerobic reactors (Nagano & Kobayashi, 1990; Wiegant & Lettinga, 1985). These wastes have been conventionally treated by adjusting their temperatures to a mesophilic anaerobic pro- cess. Thermophilically grown sludge possesses intrinsically much higher methanogenic activity than mesophilic sludge (Wiegant & de Man, 1986). Therefore, it is definitely more rational to treat these high-temperature wastes by a thermophilic process. In this study we adopted an alcohol distillery vinasse as a typical high-temperature wastewater containing a large amount of poorly biodegradable matter, in order to investigate the feasibility of a thermophilic UASB process. A long-term experi- ment was made over 430 days using a 140 1 UASB reactor having a modified gas-solids separator. This paper describes the reactor performance with respect to COD and BOD elimination, along with the microbial characteristics of the thermophilically grown sludge. 216 H. Harada, S. Uemura, A.-C. Chen, J. Jayadevan METHODS Experimental apparatus Figure 1 shows the UASB reactor used. The reactor was made of stainless steel. The void volume of the reactor was 140 1, consisting of a 126 1 column por- tion (20 cm in ID and 4 m in height) and a 14 1 gas-solids separator (GSS). A modification was made in the GSS portion by installing four inclined plates at 60 in order to minimize carry-over of suspended sludge. A skimmer was also provided at the liquid-gas interface in the GSS, which worked at 120 rpm for 5 rain at 20 min intervals, to prevent scum accumulation. The reactor was kept at 55 by a water-jacket. A total amount of 87 1 of thermophilic sludge with 12000 mg volatile suspended solids (VSS) 1-~ was used as a seed material. The sludge was harvested from a suspended-growth-type digester at the same plant from which the alcohol distillery waste used in this study was obtained. 12 Fig. 1. Experimental set-up. 1, Substrate reservoir; 2, mixer; 3, feeding pump; 4, inlet; 5, recirculation pump; 6, sampling ports; 7, gas deflector; 8, inclined plates; 9, scum breaker; 10, outlet; 11, gas trap; 12, wet gas meter; 13, gas exit; 14, water jacket; 15, temperature sensor; 16, tem- perature controller; 17, hot-water tank; 18, hot-water recirculation pump. Increments in volumetric COD loading rate were made stepwise by shortening HRT, both when the effluent COD became stable and the effluent acetate was steady at less than 200 mg COD 1-1 for at least 1 week (Wiegant & de Man, 1986). The volumetric loading and HRT described in this paper are based on the total reactor volume, including the GSS volume. Feed A cane molasses vinasse used for most of the test was obtained from an alcohol distillery plant in Thailand, and the vinasse used for the comparison test came from a malt-whisky distillery in Japan. The representative characteristics of the raw wastewater are presented in Table 1. The raw wastewater was diluted ten-fold with tap water, in order to adjust the influent COD strength to approximately 10 g COD 1-1. The influent total COD and soluble COD were 9970 mg COD 1-~ (SD = 1170) and 8340 mg COD 1-1 (SD = 947), respectively, during the experi- mental period. The influent total BOD and soluble BOD were 2490 mg BOD 1-1 (SD = 668) and 2060 mg BOD 11 (SD =567). Hence, this waste was characterized by an extremely low BOD/COD ratio. Basal nutrients and trace elements were added to the vinasse according to Wiegant and Lettinga (1985). NaHCO3, as buffer, was added to the influ- ent at a concentration of 5 g 1-~. As a result, the influent pH was maintained at around 7.3 through- out the entire experiment. Serum vial test for methane productivity Two kinds of serum vial tests were conducted: one for assessment of the temperature response of the methanogenic activity of the thermophilic granular sludge, and the other for examination of the bio- degradability of the waste used. For the methanogenic activity test, sludge was taken out from the second lowest sampling tap of the reactor on day 230. The sludge was disintegrated using a Physcotron blender for 1 min at dial 40 under nitrogen purging, and then washed with 0.05 Table 1. A 40 ml cell suspension in the buffer was transferred into 120 ml in each vial. A portion (10 ml) of anaerobically prepared stock solution, which contained basal nutrients, reducing agent (NazS.9H20, at a final concentration of 250 mg 1-1), resazurin (at a final concentration of 1 mg 1-1) was added. Finally, liquid substrates (acetate, or the vinasse) were added to each vial. The liquid sub- strate concentration was set at 2000 mg 1-1 vial liquid. The head space of each vial (70 ml) was filled with Oz-free N2 gas in the case of liquid substrates. For determination of hydrogenotrophic activity, Hz/ COz (80:20%, v/v) was filled at 1.5 atm into the head space instead of liquid substrate. Methane produc- tion was estimated by measurement of gas production and composition at regular intervals. The test was conducted in a reciprocal shaker at five different temperatures in the range of 35-65. The biodegradability of the vinasse waste was evaluated by comparison of the methane production rates between the waste and other reference sub- strates; acetate, H2/COz, glucose. For comparison, another type of vinasse was tested, which derived from an alcohol (whisky) distillery that used malt as the raw material for fermentation. A mesophilic granular sludge was used which was harvested from a UASB reactor receiving a mixture of sucrose and VFA operated at a volumetric loading rate of 20 kg COD m-3 d1 at 35. All procedures were the same as those used in the determination of the methano- genic activity test, other than the test temperature, at 35. Analysis Biogas composition was determined with a gas chro- matograph (Shimadzu GC 15-A) equipped with a thermal conductivity detector. The column used was Molecular Sieve 5A 60/80 mesh (1500 mm 3 mm ID). The column oven and detector were held at 55 and l l0, respectively. Helium was used as the carrier gas at a flow rate of 40 ml min ~. The gas volume was determined by a wet-test gas meter. Sul- fide in the biogas was determined by an iodometric method (APHA, 1985) after absorption in a zinc acetate solution. Volatile fatty acid (VFA) composi- tion was analyzed by a gas chromatograph (Shimadzu GC14-A) equipped with a flame ionized detector. A glass column (held at 175) with Car- bopak B-DA/4% (80/120 mesh) was used. The detector and injection port were held at 190. Nitrogen was used as the carrier gas at a flow rate of 50 ml min-l. Sulfate, sulfide, COD, BOD and the other analyses were made according to Standard Methods (APHA, 1985). Prior to COD determina- tion, samples were acidified and purged with N2 gas to cancel sulfide interference. The soluble COD was determined after passing through a 0.45 membrane filter. RESULTS Reactor performance The performance of the thermophilic UASB reactor with respect to COD removal is given in Fig. 2. The COD loading rate was increased stepwise from 2.4 to 28 kg COD m-3 d-I until day 160 by reducing the HRT. The loading was then lowered to 19 kg COD m-3 d-1 because of the gradual deterioration of COD removal. On day 325, it was raised to 24 kg COD m-3 d-1. Accordingly, the entire period was divided into 7 phases [Fig. 2(b)]. A sharp decline in the effluent COD occurred after day 50 [Fig. 2(c)]. In the period of days 50-160, COD removal tended to worsen as the loading increased from 4.1 to 28 kg COD m-3 d-1 [Fig. 2(a) and (b)]. A reduction in COD loading to 19 kg COD m-3 d-~ in the following period caused a slight improvement in COD removal, but the reactor responded to a subsequent increment of the loading to 24 kg COD m-3 d-1 at day 326, with a deteriora- tion of COD removal until the end of the experiment. As a whole, the COD removals based on influent-total versus effluent-soluble, i.e. Remt_s, decreased from 70 to 40%, and that on the basis of in fluent-total versus effluent-total, i.e. Remt_t, decreased from 60 to 20%. Determinations of BOD were conducted starting from day 206 onwards (Fig. 3). A mesophilically grown granular sludge was used as a non-acclima- tized seed source (Fig. 7). The most rapid conversion was observed in vials filled with either H2/CO2 or acetate, achieving 2.3 kg CH4-COD kg VSS-1 d-1 and 2.0, respectively. The methane production rate from the malt-vinasse was almost equivalent to that from glucose, lying in the range 1.5-1.6 kg CH4-COD kg VSS-~ d-~. DISCUSSION From the results of the continuous-flow experiments, the BOD removal efficiencies in the last two phases in which BOD data are available (at loading rates of 19 and 24 kg COD m-s d-1) were high. In terms of Remt_~, COD removal was 39-45%, whereas BOD removal achieved was mostly above 80%. A similar tendency, that despite a low COD removal a high BOD removal is achieved, has been reported in the anaerobic treatment of alcohol wastewaters by other investigators (Nagano & Kobayashi, 1990; Romero et al., 1990). The BOD/ COD ratio in the last two phases was 0.24-0.27 for the influent, and 0.046-0.085 for the effluent. This denotes that refractory matters constitute a large fraction of the vinasse COD, and that the biodegrad- able matters could be almost removed by the thermophilic UASB. The biodegradability test (Fig. 7) disclosed that only 10% of the initially added COD was converted to methane in the vial that contained the vinasse, whereas more than 60% was 1.2 _ 0.8 0.4 0.0 0.2 0.4 0.6 Time (day) Fig. 7. Jayadevan converted in the malt-vinasse vial. This suggests that the biodegradability of distillery wastewater varies considerably from one plant to another according to the origin of fermentation materials and the distilla- tion process. Some organic compounds, such as phenolic compounds, present in vinasse, which are produced through oxidation and cause a dark brown color (Wiegant & Lettinga, 1985) are reported to be not only refractory but also toxic for methanogens (Field et al., 1989). These compounds were probably the cause of the poor reactor performance for COD. SEM observations demonstrated that Methanosar- cina-like coccoids were present in abundance, whereas Methanothrix-like bamboo-shaped rods existed to a far smaller extent. It is well known that the predominance of Methanothrix in granular sludge is most essential for the establishment of a high- performance UASB process (Hulshoff Pol et al., 1983). Although we attempted to induce the preva- lence of Methanothrix according to the start-up guideline proposed by Wiegant & de Man (1986), the bacterium did not become a predominant methanogen in our thermophilic granules. Probably, thermophilic Methanothrix is more sensitive to the refractory/toxic compounds in the vinasse than is the thermophilic Methanosarcina. Recently, the predominance of Methanosarcina in thermophilic granular sludge has been reported (Rintala et al., 1993; Ahring et al., 1993). Ahring and co-workers (Schmidt & Ahring, 1993; Schmidt et al., 1992; Ahring et al., 1993) reported that a high con- centration of bivalent cations, such as Mg2+ and Ca2+, induced development of single cells of the Methanosarcina species, which are more easily washed out from the UASB reactor than large clumps or packets. The influent in this study con- tained a relatively low level of bivalent cation (approximately 1.1 mm of Mg2+ and 1.5 mm of Ca2+), at which level the development of Methano- sarcina clumps might be enhanced. As a result of retainment of the bacterial clumps, Methanosarcina- rich granules could develop in our UASB system. The granules had a mean size of 1.5 ram, and were somewhat fragile and irregular in shape. The sludge volume index (SVI) of the granulated sludge ranged between 20 and 45 ml g VSS-1. The temperature optimum for growth of thermo- philic Methanosarcina was reported to be in the range of 50-58, while that for thermophilic Metha- nothrix ranged from 60-65 (Van Lier et al., 1993). This coincides with the previous findings that the temperature optimum for acetoclastic (methano- genic) activity of Methanothrix-rich thermophilic granules lay in the range of 60-65 (Van Lier et al., 1992; 1993; Uemura & Harada, 1993), while that for thermophilic sludge in which Methanosarcina was predominant was rather lower at 50-58 (Zinder et al., 1984). Our vinasse-grown thermophilic granules showed the highest acetate-utilizing methanogenic activity at 60, and it decreased at 65 (Fig. 6), accounting for the above-mentioned microscopic observation. Previous reports described Methanobac- terium thermoautotrophicum as tending to be a predominant hydrogenotrophic methanogen in ther- mophilic granular consortia (Visser et al., 1991; Van Lier et al., 1992). The temperature optimum of this bacterium lies in the range of 65-70 (Zeikua & Wolfe, 1972). The temperature optimum for hydro- genotrophic methanogenic activity of our thermophilic granules was around 65 (Fig. 6), which corresponds to that for Methanobacterium thermoautotrophicum. The methanogenic activity from the vinasse was found to be highest at 55. The overall methane production from the vinasse can be accomplished by consecutive reactions of various groups of thermo- philic anaerobic bacteria which might have different temperature optima. The fact that the optimum temperature of methane production from the vinasse was different from those from H2/CO2 and from acetate suggests that the rate-limiting step of the overall vinasse degradation did not consist of the final methanogenesis from either H2/CO2 or from acetate, but in the degradation of intermediate products such as propionate. Van Lier et al. (1993) found that the optimum temperature for propionate conversion in thermophilic granules was 55-60, supporting this hypothesis. Furthermore, cautious inspection of Fig. 6 and Fig. 7 shows an interesting interference. At 55 the methanogenic activity of thermophilic sludge from the vinasse was about 2/3 that from acetate (Fig. 6). In contrast, the methano- genic activity of the unacclimatized sludge (mesophilic granules) from the vinasse was only 1/32 of that from acetate (Fig. 7). ce:abstract-sec.ce:simple-para:
The feasibility of thermophilic (55°C) anaerobic treatment of an alcohol distillery wastewater (cane molasses vinasse) was studied using a 140 l upflow anaerobic sludge blanket (UASB) reactor for a period of 430 days. Organic loading rates were applied up to 28 kg chemical oxygen demand (COD) m−3 d−1 by reducing hydraulic retention time (HRT) at a fixed influent concentration of 10 g COD l−1. Chemical oxygen demand removals during the entire experimental period were relatively low (39–67%), while biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) removals were more satisfactory (more than 80%). The biodegradability of the vinasse used in this study was assessed by a serum vial test. The test revealed that methane production rates from the vinasse were only

H 2
